conventions.convention: Hilbert spaces are nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. Entropy uses natural logarithms, is dimensionless in nats, and assigns 0 log 0 = 0. Physical entropy is k_B times dimensionless entropy.

Support is the orthogonal complement of the kernel. Relative entropy is defined for positive semidefinite operators, without a normalization requirement, using support-restricted spectral logarithms when support inclusion holds and +∞ otherwise.
Partial traces contract the indicated ordered tensor factor and retain the remaining factors in their displayed order. I(A:C|B) = S(ρ_AB) + S(ρ_BC) − S(ρ_B) − S(ρ_ABC).

Channel monotonicity is a finite-dimensional, one-sided inequality for every positive semidefinite input pair. It asserts no equality characterization, recovery map, or infinite-dimensional extension.

The thermal bound assumes Choice and β > 0. Its lattice boundary size counts crossing interaction labels, rather than boundary sites. Empty tensor products are C. The family conclusion requires the explicit uniform bound ||H_boundary,s|| ≤ C |boundary A_s| and makes no additional geometric scaling claim.

load_bearing.statement: For finite density operators, S(ρ) = −Σ_{λ_j>0} λ_j log λ_j; I(A:B)_ρ = S(ρ_A) + S(ρ_B) − S(ρ_AB); I(A:C|B)_ρ = S(ρ_AB) + S(ρ_BC) − S(ρ_B) − S(ρ_ABC), using natural logarithms and the displayed ordered partial traces.

For a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional ordered triple, I(A:C|B)_ρ ≥ 0. For d,e ≥ 1, every CPTP map Φ:M_d(C)→M_e(C), and all positive semidefinite X,Y∈M_d(C), D(Φ(X)||Φ(Y)) ≤ D(X||Y), including extended-real support-failure cases.

Assume Choice. For nonzero finite-dimensional complex factor spaces, Hermitian H_A,H_B,H_boundary, H = H_A⊗I_B + I_A⊗H_B + H_boundary, and β > 0, the Gibbs density ρ_β = e^(−βH)/Tr(e^(−βH)) satisfies I(A:B)_{ρ_β} ≤ 2β||H_boundary||_op. For the specified finite lattice family, ||H_boundary,s||_op ≤ C|boundary A_s| implies I(A_s:B_s)_{ρ_βs} ≤ 2β_s C|boundary A_s| memberwise.
